title: HBOPPPS hybrid teaching model with online resource library for Physiology at Harbin Medical University
description: HBOPPPS is a hybrid teaching method introduced in 2019 that incorporates online instructional techniques into the offline BOPPPS framework (Bridge-in, Objective, Pre-assessment, Participatory learning, Post-assessment, Summary). The team built an online resource set including "course-associated micro-lecture videos (85 in total, 5 ∼ 10 min/video)", science stories, lectures by renowned doctors, virtual simulation experiments and chapter tests. Pre-class course guidance was delivered through the "Xuexi Tong" mobile application, with in-class interactive elements such as sign-in procedures, multi-choice questions and task allocation.
requirements: An established offline BOPPPS teaching model
An online learning resource library and a mobile application for course guidance and interaction
constraints: Implemented for Physiology teaching at Harbin Medical University among undergraduate medical students
target_learners: Undergraduate medical students in Pharmacy, Clinical Pharmacy, Basic Medicine and Clinical Medicine programs
target_learning_goals: Understanding healthy human body functions in Physiology, linking preclinical and clinical courses
examples: Students received pre-class course guidance via the Xuexi Tong app covering course objectives and key knowledge, and used in-class online sign-in, quiz and response functions

article_title: Assessment of the effectiveness of BOPPPS-based hybrid teaching model in physiology education.
citation: Liu Xiao-Yu, Lu Chunmei, Zhu Hui, Wang Xiaoran, Jia Shuwei, Zhang Ying, Wen Haixia, Wang Yu-Feng. (2022). Assessment of the effectiveness of BOPPPS-based hybrid teaching model in physiology education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-022-03269-y
title: HBOPPPS: a hybrid BOPPPS teaching model delivered through the Xuexi Tong mobile app in three stages
description: HBOPPPS is a hybrid teaching method that incorporates online teaching into the six BOPPPS components, delivered through the "Xuexi Tong" mobile app. It operates in three stages: before the lecture (posted guidance, 80 micro-lecture videos of 5–10 min, opening questions, science stories and clinical cases), during the lecture (app sign-in, bridge-in stimuli, app-administered pre-assessment with automatic answer statistics, participatory learning with group discussion and student presentations, post-assessment with 3–5 multi-choice questions, and summary), and after the lecture (a teacher-posted mind map, student-posted course summaries, and online question-and-answer discussion). The app also generates an online score of students' learning initiatives.
requirements: Students are required to watch the micro-lecture videos completely before the lecture, and the model depends on the mobile app for sign-in, quiz administration, automatic answer statistics, and online discussion
constraints: The article notes minor differences in HBOPPPS components among different teachers, such as options for interpreting the micro-video lecture or using pre-assessment with the quiz following the bridge-in
target_learning_goals: systematic learning of Physiology course content
examples: Before introducing respiratory functions, teachers mentioned respiratory symptoms of COVID-19 patients or broadcast a heavy breathing sound to attract students' attention; a smartphone shake randomly selected students to answer questions
